newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves VSNL cable investment.
newsitem.headline: India approves VSNL cable investment.

text.p: The Indian government on Monday approved a proposal by state-owned international telecommunications company Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) to participate in the SEA-ME-WE 3 underwater cable system.
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a 1.85-billion rupee investment by VSNL in the project, including a foreign exchange component of 1.68 billion.
The committee authorised VSNL to carry out all legal and other formalities for participation in the SEA-ME-WE 3 cable system.

The SEA-ME-WE 3 system is an optical fibre undersea cable system connecting South East Asia, the Indian subcontinent, the Middle East, North Africa and Western Europe. The cable will cross over land in Egypt.
The cable system will have 39 landing points in 33 countries, and will allow VSNL to acquire transmission capacity to meet projected traffic beginning in the 1998/99 (April-March) fiscal year.
